lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: informal comparative inference

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: Sample A: 20, 22, 21, 23. Sample B: 15, 17, 16, 14. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?

steps: Find the mean of Sample A: (20 + 22 + 21 + 23) ÷ 4 = 86 ÷ 4 = 21 1/2.
Find the mean of Sample B: (15 + 17 + 16 + 14) ÷ 4 = 62 ÷ 4 = 15 1/2.
Since 21 1/2 > 15 1/2, Sample A tends to have greater values.
workedSolution.answer: Sample A, with a mean of 21 1/2 compared to 15 1/2.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Sample A: 19, 21, 22, 21, 23. Sample B: 14, 11, 22, 26, 18. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Both samples have the same range.
Sample A, with a range of 15 compared to 4.
Sample B, with a range of 15 compared to 4.
Sample A, with a range of 4 compared to 15.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 564 commuters on a train line. She randomly selects 108 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: All 564 commuters on a train line
Only the first 108 commuters on a train line on a list
The 108 randomly selected commuters on a train line

items.prompt: A student uses a random number generator to select 73 shoppers at a grocery store from the full list, then surveys them. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.
No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 18 commuters on a train line, 5 preferred an extended weekend event. Based on this sample, about how many of the 144 commuters on a train line would you expect to prefer an extended weekend event?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 44, 33, 35, 42, 40. What is the range of these sample estimates?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A population has 3828 students at Lincoln Middle School. Student A takes a random sample of 20. Student B takes a random sample of 38. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
